questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to visit Australia and found exchange to be a perfect opportunity for that. I specifically chose Melbourne because I have heard that it is a very nice city to live and study in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I highly recommend going on exchange! It's a great opportunity to break away from your normal everyday life and experience something new. Melbourne has been an amazing base as it is a lovely city to live in with many amazing travel destinations nearby, both within Victoria and throughout the rest of Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found this part quite easy. The University of Melbourne was good at sending emails before arrival with all the information you needed to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: On the 'Welcome Day' all exchange students attended a presentation where important information about studying at the University of Melbourne was provided. Additionally, you could always visit the student service 'Stop One' on campus for assistance with course planning or any other questions related to student life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my accommodation through a Facebook group created for University of Copenhagen students going to Australia, where another Danish girl had secured an apartment through her friend who had been on exchange in Melbourne the semester before us - so I was very lucky to find a place before arrival!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I know that many other exchange students started by staying in an Airbnb for the first couple of weeks and found a place after arriving. Most chose off-campus housing, as the on-campus options were very expensive and not particularly appealing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very happy with the place I stayed, but I know others felt that the prices were far too expensive for what they got in return.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found this part easy! University of Melbourne was great at communicating what needed to be done.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you needed help, you could always email the university both before and after arrival. I remember they responded quite quickly! After arriving, you could also book an appointment at Stop One, the university's student service centre.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Handbook is very useful tool for exploring all the courses offered by the University of Melbourne - take some time to search through it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses were interesting, and I had some great lecturers, but compared to the University of Copenhagen, I would say the academic level was not as high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My courses included a mix of lectures and tutorials with class discussions, so it was quite similar to University of Copenhagen. However, one difference was that all lectures were livestreamed, which meant that many students didn't attend lectures in person. Another difference was that most of my courses required students to attend at least 80% of their tutorials to pass the subject.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Living in a Risk Society, Melbourne: Urban Anthropology in Action, Punishment and Social Control and Street Art

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found all my courses interesting! They were also quite manageable in terms of workload, as all of them had assignments during the semester instead of a final exam.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The OSHC (an obligatory health insurance) - there are different providers, and I personally chose the cheapest option, which costed 1,523 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying food in supermarkets was more expensive than I expected, but otherwise, most other things were pretty much as I had imagined – though I did expect Australia to be expensive. I highly recommend taking advantage of the University of Melbourne's free food options! You can pick up three free frozen meals every week, enjoy free breakfast on campus a couple of days a week, and collect a free box of fruits and vegetables every other week, if I remember correctly. Traveling around Australia is also very expensive – I was especially surprised by how expensive accommodations, such as hostels, are.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne offers many different clubs, such as surf club, mountaineering club, coffee club and wine society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join a club, but I did attend some of the events organised by Musex (the club for exchange students), which was a great way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In Victoria I would recommend to visit Wilsons Prom, Great Ocean Road, Grampians and Phillip Island. Additionally I have really enjoyed visiting Tasmania, the East Coast, Northern Territory and New Zealand. I can recommend to rent a campervan - it is such a nice way to travel around in Australia and New Zealand!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is not that different from Copenhagen, so I found it have been pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I ended up getting to know most local students through my courses. However, I found it easier to become friends with other exchange students. I heard from others that joining clubs and living with Australians can be a great way to connect! :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't found any cultural differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the vibe in Fitzroy, where I lived - lots of great shops, cafes and bars! And the coffee is so good - however, be prepared for most coffee shops in Australia to close around 2 pm in the afternoon :((

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I was very happy that the courses I chose didn't have any final exams, as it gave me more time to travel after the semester. However, it did mean a slightly heavier workload during the semester, but it was still manageable. Winter in Australia can be surprisingly cold, and the weather in Melbourne is generally very unpredictable, so be sure to pack a variety of clothing. Australia is also quite expensive, so try to save up as much money as possible. I'd highly recommend starting early with scholarship applications - it's a time-consuming process, and many scholarships close for applications early. Start as soon as you've secured your spot!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of other Danes on exchange in Melbourne, and it's very easy to stay within that bubble. If you want to make more international friends, you'll need to actively seek out those opportunities, such as by joining clubs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great people I have met and all the amazing places I have visit both during the semester and after it ended! I've also really enjoyed having more free time and being able to be more spontaneous.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes being so far away from home, friends, and family can be challenging, but most of the time, it's absolutely worth it!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I cannot recommend going on exchange at the University of Melbourne enough! If you're considering it - do it! Melbourne is an incredible city to live in, and Australia is an amazing country to travel around.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
